todays_decisions.reasoning: I accept the Market Analyst's low-confidence risk-on lean (0.4): SPY is 3.44% above its 200-day, RSP leads, and VIXY is unwinding. Rising long yields and Nvidia's print on 11-17 are the reasons to stay measured. I approve MCO at $25 (P1), cut VTI from $25 to $15 (P2) and approve the full BND sale (P3). Net, about $40 of a beta-0.1 bond reserve moves into $40 of US equity in favored or preferred areas. Cash ends near $86 (about 13.6%), roughly where it started. The 10%-drop stress moves from about -$22.0 to about -$24.4, against the Implicator's -$25.4 for the full set. P2 is sized down on the Skeptic's timing point: the Proposer himself says a one-day delay costs little, so I buy half before Nvidia's print and leave room for the rest. The owner's goal of being mostly invested within about a week is in my role brief, which answers the Skeptic's point (1). The remaining roughly $23 above the 10% buffer goes into US core or a favored-sector name after the 11-17 and 11-19 prints. That keeps the 11-13 commitment (L4); if I don't deploy it then, I owe a new, specific reason. L4: VTI follows the Market Analyst's 'US core is the place to be long' call and is not a diversification-only token, but it reverses VTI's stored 'no adds' line, and I say so in its thesis. L3: MCO and MSCI are one financial-data sleeve (about 8.3% of equity), and MSCI's thesis now says so. L2: MCO's next date (2027-02-17) is from the News Analyst's filings check. Its 11-13 8-K 8.01 is only inferred to be the euro notes deal, which is minor for a $25 position. L8 and L7 on BND: its stored thesis says it is not a hedge and names it the next sale if the hike path pushes yields higher. Two hikes are now priced and the 10-year is at 5.15%, so that condition has happened, even though the measurable IEF more-than-3%-below-200-day test is untripped (IEF is 2.26% below; TLT is 4.03% below). The stop is NEAR (+0.8%). The sale is tax-clean (both lots short-term, about -$0.36), and in its 'reserve' role BND only duplicates cash. The Skeptic said he would not object to the sale with P2 deferred, and P2 is half-sized. Held-book review (L7, from the stop blocks): no price stop has tripped. Only BND is NEAR, and it is being sold. Qualitative clauses: WMT's XLP 21d is +6.54%, above +3%, with no guidance cut before 11-19. VOO's RSP 21d is +2.87%, positive, with SPY 3.44% over its 200-day. INCY's MAESTRA-3 Phase 3 cancellation (8-K 8.01, 11-13) is a dropped planned study with guidance kept, not a failed pivotal trial or a guidance cut, so it is untripped. EXEL's Morgan Stanley $57 target is not an 8-K event, so it is untripped, but there are no Health Care adds. KR's cyber incident is unconfirmed. CARG, DPZ, IDXX, MSCI and VRSN have no guidance cut or negative filing. FAST has no report before 2027-01-19. WMT's 8-K 5.02 filed 11-16 is unread from item numbers three sessions before its print. No proposal lets me trim further, so its $119 stop stands, and the Proposer should bring a WMT reduction tomorrow if the filing turns out to be a senior executive departure. L6 fixes in thesis_updates: EXEL's stop text is now measured from the $69.04 fill, KR's from the $67.06 blended cost, and VOO's SPY 200-day is re-dated to 729.31 (11-13 close). MCO has no price in my inputs, so its stop text is written against the recorded fill rather than the 11-10 menu close. The $470 figure is a placeholder, as is the $345 VTI clause, measured from an assumed blended cost near $375.
